top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a specific, mature, cleanly attributed achievement: the optical lattice clock, in which neutral atoms trapped at a magic wavelength cancel the lattice light shift, taken by Katori and Ye to about 1e-18 fractional uncertainty. The accuracy rests on quantitatively controlled atomic-structure shifts (blackbody, hyperfine, higher-order light and collisional) and has been confirmed by several independent laboratories. Two names map onto the invention and the accuracy record, and the citation scoped to the neutral-atom lattice scheme answers the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control overlap. P002 is a genuinely strong second, with a predicted and then observed new platform, but it is about eight years old, the pairing mechanism is open and first-author and parallel-group credit falls outside three names, so I rank it behind P001 and ahead of no award.
recusal_note: No recusal need apparent from profile: none of Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer is among my documented collaborators. I work in atomic theory close to the precision-metrology community and have long collaborated with Anne L'Huillier, Lund and ETH Zurich groups on attosecond physics, none of whom are credited on P001 or P002.
